text: Structures $\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{N}$ are elementarily equivalent ($\mathcal{M} \equiv \mathcal{N}$) precisely when:
choices: $\mathrm{Th}(\mathcal{M}) = \mathrm{Th}(\mathcal{N})$, i.e. they satisfy the same first-order sentences
one elementarily embeds into the other
explanation: By definition $\mathcal{M} \equiv \mathcal{N}$ means $\mathrm{Th}(\mathcal{M}) = \mathrm{Th}(\mathcal{N})$. Isomorphism implies elementary equivalence but is strictly stronger, since upward Lowenheim-Skolem produces elementarily equivalent, non-isomorphic models. Equal cardinality is neither necessary nor sufficient, and an elementary embedding is a map rather than this equivalence relation.
